new.S1-R1: A checkbox field will offer an authoring option, "Note required if Monitor / Not OK"
new.S1-R2: The option will be on by default for newly added checkbox fields, starters included
new.S1-R3: When the option is on and the technician selects Monitor or Not OK, a note will be required before the inspection can be submitted
new.S1-R4: The system will enforce the requirement on submit, not only while the technician is filling the form
new.S1-R5: Before submit, the technician will see the field listed among the outstanding items, so they are not rejected by an error they could have avoided
new.S1-R6: The same option will apply to per-axle measurement fields
new.S1-R7: On a per-axle field the requirement is triggered by the verdicts recorded on the positions, not by an axle's stored roll-up. A single Not OK tire will require the note as soon as it is set
new.S1-N1: If the option is off, a Monitor or Not OK response with no note will submit successfully
new.S1-N2: If the response is OK or N/A, no note will be required
new.S1-E1: A note containing only spaces counts as empty
new.S1-E2: Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author opens one and turns the option on
new.S1-E3: If the option is turned on while an inspection is already in progress, that inspection keeps the rule it started with
new.S1-E4: If the technician writes a note and then changes the response to OK, the note is kept
new.S1-E5: On a per-axle field, the requirement triggers when any axle is marked Monitor or Not OK
new.S1-E7: A per-axle field whose positions all read OK will not require a note, even if an axle carried a flagged roll-up from an earlier response shape
new.S1-E6: If the field has no label, the outstanding-items list still identifies it by its type and position rather than showing an empty row
new.S17-R1: A checkbox field will offer an authoring option, "Photo required if Not OK"
new.S17-R2: The option will be off by default for newly added checkbox fields, starters included
new.S17-R3: When the option is on and the technician selects Not OK, at least one photo will be required before the inspection can be submitted
new.S17-R4: The system will enforce the requirement on submit, not only while the technician is filling the form
new.S17-R5: Before submit, the technician will see the field listed among the outstanding items, so they are not rejected by an error they could have avoided
new.S17-R6: The option applies to checkbox fields only. A per-axle field records a verdict per position, and there is no single position a photo of the field would belong to
new.S17-R7: The option is separate from "Photo required", which asks for a photo whatever the response. When both are on the unconditional rule is the one the technician is held to, and the summary sentence in the builder says so
new.S17-R8: The photo target is offered rather than always shown. Add Photo sits in the field card footer beside Add Note and the target opens on it, or on its own the moment a response makes a photo required, so the technician never has to look for it
new.S17-R9: Inspection photographs will accept HEIC as well as JPEG and PNG. A phone camera producing HEIC must not be able to make S17-R3 unsatisfiable. Where the format cannot be rendered in place, the viewer says so and offers the download, as S11-R9 already does for reference files
new.S17-N1: If the option is off, a Not OK response with no photo will submit successfully
new.S17-N2: OK, Monitor and N/A never require a photo. Monitor requires a note, not a photograph
new.S17-N3: Templates created before this release are unaffected until an author opens one and turns the option on
new.S17-E1: If the technician attaches a photo and then changes the response to OK, the photo is kept
new.S17-E2: If the technician satisfies the rule and then removes the photo, the field blocks submit again
new.S17-E3: If the option is turned on while an inspection is already in progress, that inspection keeps the rule it started with
new.S17-E4: If photo upload is unavailable to the shop, the technician is told why rather than being blocked by a requirement with no visible cause
new.S17-E5: If the field has no label, the outstanding-items list identifies it by its type and position rather than showing an empty row
new.S17-E6: If a photograph is rejected for its format, the technician is told which formats are accepted at the point of failure rather than being left with a generic upload error
new.S2-R0: Building lines requires ShopCoach. Without it the completed inspection offers the report and a link to its work order, and no build action at all
new.S2-R1: Every Monitor and Not OK finding will be represented by at least one line. ShopCoach composes each line's name, description, time estimate and parts; the field label, the measured value and the technician's note are inputs to that drafting rather than the line text itself (S15). When drafting fails, S15-E2 applies instead
new.S2-R2: A generated line will behave as an ordinary work order line from that point on, indistinguishable from one a user typed
new.S2-R3: The user will choose the target before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order
new.S2-R4: The system will offer the work order the inspection was run on only while that work order is an eligible build target. Eligible means Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review, and no invoice exists. This document does not describe a work order as open or closed: the platform carries several competing definitions of open, and this rule names its own predicate rather than joining them
new.S2-R5: When the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, the destination menu still opens and offers only a new work order. It is ineligible when its status is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or when an invoice already exists. Declined counts as ineligible because lines added to a refused order would revive work the customer turned down
new.S2-R6: A new work order will be created for the same customer and asset as the work order the inspection was run on, using their current values
new.S2-R7: When the lines are added, they will arrive approved or awaiting authorisation according to the shop's existing setting for automatically approving work order lines, exactly as a manually added line does
new.S2-R8: A work order in Approved status will not require re-approval, because approval applies to lines rather than to the work order
new.S2-R9: A generated line will take the shop's default labour type, and where no default is set, the first labour type available to the shop. The labour rate will follow from the labour type. This is stated as a rule of its own rather than as a reference to the manual New Line form, whose fallback is behaviour of that form and not of the server
new.S2-R10: The time estimate ShopCoach proposes will be carried onto the line, and will be editable before the line is added. Where no estimate is proposed the line arrives at zero, to be estimated by whoever plans the work
new.S2-R11: The user will arrive on the target work order's Lines tab as soon as the target is chosen, before the drafting has finished, and will watch it complete there
new.S2-R12: Once the lines have been added, the inspection will no longer count as needing a work order. Drafting alone does not change that state, because a draft the user abandoned left the findings unactioned
new.S2-R13: An inspection is built from once. After lines have been added from it, to this work order or to a new one, no entry point offers the build action again: the completed inspection, the work order note and the asset row show the outcome instead, with a link to the work order that got the lines. The check is made again when Add Lines is pressed; if the inspection was built from elsewhere in the meantime, nothing is added and the user is told where the lines went
new.S2-R14: The destination will be chosen from a menu on the build action itself rather than from a dialog raised before it. The menu lists this work order — by number and status — and a new one seeded with the customer and unit. Either target goes straight to the drafting
new.S2-R16: The build action will have one appearance wherever it is met — the ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu
new.S2-R17: Every rule in this document that withholds an action is enforced by the server. A request made without the permission is refused, whatever the interface showed. Hiding a control is how a rule is presented, not how it is enforced. This is stated once and applies to every story — the build, the destination choice, the asset Inspections tab, template authoring and Preview. The precedent is SV-7932, where a view-only user could invoke the ShopCoach line builder because only the button had been hidden
new.S2-R18: A generated line never arrives as a Fixed Line Total line. It is an ordinary labour-and-parts line, and switching it to a fixed total stays a deliberate act afterwards. A fixed total requires labour plus parts to equal it exactly or the line cannot be saved, and a drafted line arrives carrying both figures
new.S2-N1: If the inspection is not completed, the build will not be offered
new.S2-N2: If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the build will not be offered
new.S2-N3: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the build will not be available from any entry point
new.S2-N4: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' enabled, the option to create a new work order will not be shown. They will only be offered the option to add lines to the open work order
new.S2-N5: If the user does not have 'See Financial Data' enabled, the build is still allowed and the money is not shown. The proposed-lines panel withholds the labour rate, the labour total and the part prices, and the withholding is enforced by the server rather than by leaving the fields out of the markup. Everything else in the panel stays editable and the lines can still be added
new.S2-N6: If the shop has no labour types, the build will not run. A work order line cannot be created without a labour type or a fixed price, and S2-R18 forbids a generated line from being a Fixed Line Total, so the action states the reason rather than producing a line that cannot be saved
new.S2-E2: If a note is very long, it is given to ShopCoach whole rather than truncated before it is read
new.S2-E3: An inspection with thirty flagged findings is built without a cap and without an extra confirmation. If the assistant cannot draft that many in one run, the run is split rather than the surplus findings being dropped (S15-R14)
new.S2-E4: If the user chose to add lines to the open work order and it was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing
new.S2-E5: If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result
new.S2-E6: If two users draft from the same inspection at once, nothing is duplicated by the drafting itself, because a draft is not a work order line. When both press Add Lines, only the first adds lines; the second adds nothing and the user is told where the lines went (S2-R13)
new.S2-E7: If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept
new.S2-E9: If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again. The inspection itself is unaffected, because it belongs to the work order it was run on
new.S2-E12: If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, an inspection that has a report survives it as a read-only record (S5-E3). Lines that had been added to that work order are gone with it. The inspection does not count as needing a work order, because it can no longer be built from
new.S2-E10: Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist
new.S2-E11: If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order. Deleting a work order is usually a correction; deleting a line is somebody who read the proposed work and decided against it, and re-raising the flag would ask them to do it again
new.S3-R1: The completed inspection screen will offer a Build lines action
new.S3-R2: The action will run the build described in S2, including the choice of target work order
new.S3-R3: The action will be usable on a phone, and the technician will be able to complete the whole flow without switching device
new.S3-R4: The screen will lead with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged row as field, axle and row, followed by every flagged position on it with its reading, for example 'Brake & tire measurements · Axle 1 · Tire pressure: left outer 42 psi, right outer 40 psi'
new.S3-R5: A verdict with no findings under it will not be counted on the card. A zero reads as a finding at a glance, which is the opposite of what it says
new.S3-R6: With ShopCoach the card's footer will offer View PDF, Go to work order and Build lines, and a note above it will name the product once. Without ShopCoach the footer will offer View PDF and Go to work order, and the same space will carry a plain line saying the findings are on the customer report and in the work order note feed and that the lines are added on the work order. When the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, the footer offers View PDF only, with or without ShopCoach, and no plain line; it also shows the outcome when the lines went onto another work order that still exists (S5-E3)
new.S3-R7: The section-by-section review of what the technician entered will stay below the summary card. The card answers what happened; the sections answer what was entered. The service advisor, the inspection's start time and per-section progress are not carried onto this screen: the first two belong to the work order the inspection was run on, and progress means nothing once the inspection is locked
new.S3-R8: Once the inspection has been built from, the footer shows the outcome in place of Build lines: 'WO created S-235' or 'Lines added S-58', linking to that work order (S2-R13)
new.S3-N1: If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the action will not be shown
new.S3-N2: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the action will not be shown. It will be absent, not disabled
new.S3-N3: If the inspection is not completed, the action will not be shown
new.S3-N4: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, no build action is shown. The screen offers View PDF and a link to the work order and no build action — the action is absent, not disabled and not behind a tooltip (S2-R0)
new.S3-E1: If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, no build action is offered (S5-E3). If it was built from before the deletion, the footer shows the outcome instead (S3-R8)
new.S3-E2: If another user builds from the same inspection while this screen is open, the check in S2-R13 is based on the current state rather than the state when the screen loaded
new.S3-E3: If the inspection is reopened while the screen is open, the action disappears
new.S4-R1: The inspection report note will offer a Build lines action alongside the existing view and download actions
new.S4-R2: The action will run the build described in S2, including the choice of target work order
new.S4-R4: All actions on the note will remain reachable on a phone, wrapping rather than overflowing
new.S4-R5: Once the inspection has been built from, the note shows the outcome in place of Build lines, worded as in S3-R8 (S2-R13)
new.S4-N1: If the report recorded only passes, the action will not be shown
new.S4-N2: If the inspection has been deleted, the note remains as a record but the action will not be shown. Removing an inspection from its line, or deleting the line, deletes the inspection on purpose: it leaves the asset's Inspections tab, and its note stays on the work order marked "Inspection deleted". This is different from deleting the whole work order (S5-E3)
new.S4-N3: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the action will not be shown
new.S4-N4: If the note is being read in the work order's history view, the action will not be shown
new.S4-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, the note keeps its view and download actions and offers no build action (S2-R0)
new.S4-E1: If the work order itself is not an eligible build target, the build creates a new work order per S2-R5 and the note stays where it is
new.S5-R1: An Inspections tab will appear on the asset record, alongside Work Orders, Invoices and Notes
new.S5-R2: The tab will list every inspection linked to that asset, most recently completed first
new.S5-R3: Each row will show the inspection, its status, the completion date, the technician who signed it, the findings, the work order it was run on, the report, and an action
new.S5-R4: The inspection column will show the template name with its version beneath, which is what distinguishes repeated runs of the same template
new.S5-R5: The status column will show the inspection's own progress only, and will not also express whether work is pending
new.S5-R6: The findings column will show one item per finding type with a colour, such as 1 Not OK in red and 3 Monitor in amber
new.S5-R7: The work order column will link to the work order the inspection was run on and show its status
new.S5-R8: The report column will link to the report when one has been generated
new.S5-R9: The action column will have three states. Needs action offers the build described in S6. Done shows the outcome and links to the resulting work order, reading "WO created" when a new work order was created and "Lines added" when the lines went onto the existing one. Nothing to do shows a dash. The same wording is used wherever the outcome replaces the build action (S2-R13)
new.S5-R10: The table has no filter row. The Inspection, Status and Completed columns can be sorted. By default the most recently completed inspection comes first (S5-R2)
new.S5-R11: A summary will read "N of M have findings with no lines yet"
new.S5-R12: An inspection needs action when it was completed after this release, has at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from. An inspection completed before the release is never flagged, because the data cannot tell one somebody already handled by hand from one nobody actioned. Those stay listed on the tab, with their issues shown
new.S5-R13: Two users with different permissions viewing the same asset will see identical counts. Only the action button differs
new.S5-R14: Everything that navigates will be a link and everything that changes something will be a button
new.S5-R15: The tab will be usable on a phone. Every column's information will remain reachable and the page will not scroll sideways
new.S5-R21: The tab lists the inspections whose work order is on this asset now, so it follows the work order when the work order's asset is changed or two assets are merged. The asset an inspection was run on is also stored on the inspection when it is created, as a record. Inspections that exist before this release are backfilled from their work order's asset at migration. When the work order has been deleted, the stored asset is used (S5-E3). Merging assets moves such inspections to the surviving asset, as it moves the work orders
new.S5-R17: A response contributes one count to exactly one of Pass, Monitor or Needs attention when the field is a checkbox or a measurement and the response is Pass, Monitor or Not OK
new.S5-R19: N/A and unanswered responses contribute nothing
new.S5-R20: A per-axle measurement field contributes one count per axle, carrying that axle's worst verdict (S8-R14). A field with three axles marked OK, Monitor and Not OK contributes one pass, one monitor and one needs-attention
new.S5-N1: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — View' enabled, the Inspections tab will not appear at all. It will be absent, not empty
new.S5-N2: If the user has 'Work Orders — View' but not 'Customers — View', the asset record is unreachable and so is the tab. No alternative route is added
new.S5-N3: If the asset has no inspections, an empty state will explain so
new.S5-N4: If the user cannot build, the action column will show no button on any row
new.S5-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, the action column shows no build button on any row. The Needs action state described in S5-R9 does not arise (S2-R0)
new.S5-E1: For a not-started inspection, the completion date, technician and findings show dashes and no action is offered
new.S5-E2: A completed inspection whose responses are all N/A reads as having no issues and never needs action
new.S5-E3: If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, an inspection that has a report stays on the asset's Inspections tab as a read-only record, with a dash in the Work order column. The Action column shows the outcome only while the work order it points to exists, for example 'WO created S-200' when the lines went onto another work order; when they went onto the deleted work order itself, it shows a dash. It can be opened and its latest report downloaded. It cannot be built from, reopened or regenerated. A reopened inspection survives as its latest report: Status reads Completed, Completed shows the date of that report, and opening the row opens that report rather than the answers, which may have changed since. Deleting a work order must not delete such an inspection, its photos or its report. An inspection with no report, including one that was submitted but whose report was never generated, is deleted with its work order
new.S5-E4: If the asset has been moved to a different customer, all of its inspections are still listed. The tab is the asset's history
new.S5-E5: If the template has been archived or deleted, the row shows the template name and version as they were at the time, never "unknown"
new.S5-E6: If two inspections share a completion time, the order between them is stable rather than varying between loads
new.S5-E7: If the work order the lines were built onto is deleted and it is not the work order the inspection was run on, the row returns to Needs action rather than showing a Done state that points nowhere
new.S5-E8: An asset inspected weekly for three years has roughly 150 rows, which the list shows without paging. Above roughly 200 rows the list will need a date filter or paging, which is follow-up work
new.S6-R1: A row that needs action will offer a build action
new.S6-R2: The action will present the target choice up front as a menu rather than opening a dialog, because the user has already decided by the time they click
new.S6-R3: The menu is the shared destination menu of S2-R14, so the row offers the same two targets, worded the same way as every other entry point
new.S6-R4: The inspection's own work order is offered as a target only while it is an eligible build target, judged by its status on the row. When it is not, it is not offered (S2-R5)
new.S6-R5: The action will run the build described in S2
new.S6-R6: A row that has been built from will show its outcome instead of the action
new.S6-R7: After a successful build, the row will show its outcome instead of the action, and the counts and the summary line will update with it
new.S6-R8: Eligibility here will be identical to S2-R5, including that Complete is not eligible
new.S6-N1: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' enabled, the new-work-order target will not be offered anywhere on this tab
new.S6-N2: If the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, only the new-work-order target will be offered
new.S6-N3: If the user chose "Add lines" and the work order has since been closed, the system will explain that and create nothing
new.S6-N4: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, no build action will appear on any row
new.S6-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, neither menu option is offered on any row and no build action appears on the tab (S2-R0)
new.S6-E1: If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, the row offers no build action and its action cell shows a dash, or the outcome if it was built from before the deletion (S5-E3)
new.S6-E2: If several rows on the same asset need action, each is built separately. There is no bulk build
new.S6-E3: A user who can fill inspections but cannot create work orders, looking at a row whose work order is closed, has no available action. The row shows a dash
new.S7-R1: A note will be added to the work order the lines landed on, stating that it was built from the inspection
new.S7-R2: When the lines went onto a new work order, the note will link back to the work order the inspection was run on. If that work order was deleted after the build, the note shows its number as text, tagged 'Work order deleted', with no link
new.S7-R3: The Notes tab count will include the new note immediately
new.S7-R4: An entry reading "Built from inspection" will be added to that work order's Audit Log
new.S7-R5: The Audit Log entry will name the inspection, link to it, and name the work order the inspection was run on. If that work order was deleted after the build, its number is shown as text, with no link
new.S7-R6: Both records will be written however the build was started, from S3, S4 or S6
new.S7-R7: The Audit Log entry and the note will carry the same three facts: that the work order was built from an inspection, which inspection, and which work order the inspection was run on. Whichever a user opens, they get the same account. Neither may carry a fact the other lacks. This holds when both records exist. If one could not be written (S7-E1), the other stands alone and the failure is logged; the user is not told
new.S7-R8: Both records will state how many lines were created. The count is known when the record is written, and the scale of what was added is the first thing an advisor wants from it
new.S7-N1: If the lines went onto the work order the inspection was run on, the note will not link to that work order from itself
new.S7-N2: If the user does not have 'View History Logs' enabled, the Audit Log is not shown to them. The entry is still recorded
new.S7-E1: If either record cannot be written, the created lines are kept and the build still reports success. The lines are the valuable output
new.S7-E2: If a user deletes the note, the Audit Log entry remains
new.S7-E3: If the inspection is later deleted, the Audit Log entry keeps the inspection name as recorded, and the link fails gracefully rather than breaking the Audit Log
new.S7-E4: If the work order is later split, the note and the Audit Log entry stay on the original. The new work order carries no inspection provenance, because a split moves lines and does not copy records. The inspection's report notes are not records of the build: when a line with an inspection is split onto a new work order, those notes move with the line and are removed from the original. Work orders split before this rule keep their notes where they are
new.S15-R1: The system will compose the brief it sends to ShopCoach from the inspection itself. For each Monitor and Not OK finding it will include the field label, its section, the measured value and its unit, the verdict, and the technician's note
new.S15-R2: A per-axle finding will name its axle and its measurement row, so a proposed line can be traced back to the measurement that caused it
new.S15-R3: The brief will state what ShopCoach may not do: invent a part it was not given, turn a passing finding into a line, or leave a flagged finding unrepresented
new.S15-R4: The user will never type anything to get lines. There is no prompt, no query box and no configuration step anywhere in this flow
new.S15-R5: The action that starts the build will read as an AI action before it is pressed, carrying the purple treatment and the AI badge. The label will not name the product
new.S15-R6: ShopCoach is named in the note on the completed inspection card (S3-R6) and in the Line Builder panel's existing title. The build action and the destination menu do not name it
new.S15-R7: Drafting will start when the destination is chosen, so the navigation and the drafting happen together rather than one after the other
new.S15-R8: While the lines are being drafted, the panel will show one skeleton row per finding, because the number of findings is known before the drafted lines are
new.S15-R9: The work order will stay usable while the drafting runs
new.S15-R10: Cancelling during the drafting will leave the work order exactly as it was
new.S15-R11: Proposed lines will arrive selected, so the default is to accept them
new.S15-R12: Every proposed title, description, labour figure and part will be editable in place before the lines are added
new.S15-R13: Each proposed line will name the finding it came from
new.S15-R14: Every flagged finding will be represented by at least one proposed line however many findings there are. If the assistant cannot draft the whole set in one run, the set will be split across runs rather than the surplus being dropped
new.S15-R15: Nothing will reach the work order until Add Lines is pressed
new.S15-R16: The proposed-lines panel is shared with the Line Builder that is started from a work order with no inspection. A change made for this flow lands on that one too, and must not degrade it
new.S15-R17: The brief will be verifiable before release. A fixed set of inspections with known findings will be run through it and the drafted lines read back against them, checking that every flagged finding is represented, that no line invents a part it was not given, and that no passing finding became a line. Without that pass the brief is a guess: an assistant's output cannot be asserted the way a deterministic one can, so the only way to know a brief works is to try it on known input
new.S15-R18: The brief will follow the pattern of the ShopCoach assistant that already recommends work from an asset — the asset's own data, then the material to reason about — with the inspection's flagged findings in place of that assistant's work-order history
new.S15-R19: The brief will state the situation before the findings: an inspection of an asset in a heavy-duty repair shop, questions authored in advance by an admin, answers recorded by a technician, and every finding sent already flagged
new.S15-R20: The brief will carry the schema of the answer it expects, so the format is shown rather than described
new.S15-R21: Each proposed line will carry the identifier of the finding it came from, so the traceability S15-R13 promises survives whatever the assistant returns
new.S15-R22: The model the brief runs on is part of what is specified. The verification pass will record the brief and the model together, because the output cannot be attributed to the brief alone
new.S15-R23: The brief and the model will be changeable on the QA environment without a release, so the verification pass can iterate
new.S15-R24: Two findings will never be collapsed into one proposed line because their titles match. The panel compares proposed lines by their finding identifier while it is serving this flow, and keeps its existing comparison for the Line Builder started from a work order, which has no findings and relies on it. The shared panel is told which flow it is in rather than having its behaviour changed for both (S15-R16)
new.S15-R25: The model the brief runs on is chosen and compared outside this epic. This story specifies that the model is recorded with the brief (S15-R22), not which model it is, and the choice must not gate this work

new.S8-E3: Free text in a value reaches the report as entered, without being converted or dropped

new.S11-R1: Any question type will hold one file attachment

new.S11-R5: The attached file will be visible on the canvas on the field's row

new.S11-R8: After a template is republished, instructions in earlier published versions will still open their attachments

new.S11-N1: Video files will be rejected, with a reason shown to the author

new.S19-R19: The attached file will open full screen in the same view and close back to the exact position in the inspection, as the reference file already does. The file name is a hyperlink that opens it; there is no separate "View Instruction" button
new.S19-R20: Instruction text will never be truncated, and the author's paragraph breaks will be preserved. Long file names will shorten
new.S19-R21: Desktop and phone will be two layouts rather than one compressed. On a phone the acknowledgement takes its own full-width row below the file row, because the file row has no width to spare and the target has to be hittable with a gloved thumb
new.S19-R22: An unacknowledged required follow-up will block submit
new.S19-R23: The block will be enforced by the server. A submit made without the acknowledgement is refused whatever the interface showed
new.S19-R24: An unacknowledged required follow-up will appear in the outstanding items list alongside missing answers and missing notes, naming the kind first and then the section, the field and the verdict, and coloured by the verdict that caused it
new.S19-R25: Pressing submit with items outstanding will open that list rather than raising an error dialog. Submit is never disabled. It is named 'Submit & Generate Report' on every surface, and the list is titled 'N items before submitting'. The rule covers the submit button only; the sign-off step keeps its current labels ('Sign & generate report', 'Sign to complete', 'Confirm & lock inspection')
new.S19-R26: An unacknowledged follow-up will not block the action that completes a section. The count on that action rises and the technician may move on, per S14-R6
new.S19-R27: Preview mounts the fill screen, so no response can be given. Every configured follow-up on a field will therefore be shown at once, each naming the response it belongs to
new.S19-R28: In Preview the file is shown but cannot be opened, as for the general reference file (S12-R31). The acknowledgement will render in the inert treatment the verdict controls already use there and will take no input, per S12-R31
new.S19-R29: Preview will draw no banner explaining itself
new.S19-N1: A per-axle field will not offer follow-ups. A verdict there is recorded per position and there is no single position an instruction would belong to, which is the reason S17-R6 already gives for the photo rule
new.S19-N2: A checked follow-up with no text and no file will block publishing, with the error on the block, as S12-R12 and S12-R13 already do for an empty response label and an empty measurement row name. A draft may still be saved
new.S19-N3: The customer report shows the follow-up instruction text and its acknowledgement, with who acknowledged it and when. The attached file does not appear on the report
new.S19-N4: Neither reaches the brief sent to ShopCoach. S15-R1 is unchanged
new.S19-N5: An acknowledgement is not a finding and carries no count. S5-R17 counts responses
new.S19-E1: Changing the response clears the acknowledgement given on the previous one. Answering the same response again asks for it afresh
new.S19-E2: A follow-up added or edited after a template is republished does not reach an inspection already running, because an inspection keeps the template version it started on
new.S19-E3: The one-press Mark OK of S18 sets OK only and never overwrites a verdict already given, so it can reveal collapsed instructions but can never create an acknowledgement the technician has not seen
new.S19-E4: A very long instruction renders in full with the file row and the acknowledgement below it, unscrolled and untruncated
new.S19-E5: Where the stored file is missing while the follow-up still refers to it, opening it fails with a message rather than a broken download, as S11-E4 already requires

old.S17-E3: If the option is turned on while an inspection is already in progress, that inspection keeps the rule it started with
old.S17-E4: If photo upload is unavailable to the shop, the technician is told why rather than being blocked by a requirement with no visible cause
old.S17-E5: If the field has no label, the outstanding-items list identifies it by its type and position rather than showing an empty row
old.S17-E6: If a photograph is rejected for its format, the technician is told which formats are accepted at the point of failure rather than being left with a generic upload error
old.S2-R0: Building lines requires ShopCoach. Without it the completed inspection offers the report and a link to its work order, and no build action at all
old.S2-R1: Every Monitor and Not OK finding will be represented by at least one line. ShopCoach composes each line's name, description, time estimate and parts; the field label, the measured value and the technician's note are inputs to that drafting rather than the line text itself (S15)
old.S2-R2: A generated line will behave as an ordinary work order line from that point on, indistinguishable from one a user typed
old.S2-R3: The user will choose the target before any drafting starts: the work order the inspection was run on, or a new work order
old.S2-R4: The system will offer the work order the inspection was run on only while that work order is an eligible build target. Eligible means Estimate, Approved, In Progress or Review. This document does not describe a work order as open or closed: the platform carries several competing definitions of open, and this rule names its own predicate rather than joining them
old.S2-R5: When the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, the system will create a new work order without asking. It is ineligible when its status is Complete, Invoiced, Paid or Declined, or when an invoice already exists. Declined counts as ineligible because lines added to a refused order would revive work the customer turned down
old.S2-R6: A new work order will be created for the same customer and asset as the work order the inspection was run on, using their current values
old.S2-R7: When the lines are added, they will arrive approved or awaiting authorisation according to the shop's existing setting for automatically approving work order lines, exactly as a manually added line does
old.S2-R8: A work order in Approved status will not require re-approval, because approval applies to lines rather than to the work order
old.S2-R9: A generated line will take the shop's default labour type, and where no default is set, the first labour type available to the shop. The labour rate will follow from the labour type. This is stated as a rule of its own rather than as a reference to the manual New Line form, whose fallback is behaviour of that form and not of the server
old.S2-R10: The time estimate ShopCoach proposes will be carried onto the line, and will be editable before the line is added. Where no estimate is proposed the line arrives at zero, to be estimated by whoever plans the work
old.S2-R11: The user will arrive on the target work order's Lines tab as soon as the target is chosen, before the drafting has finished, and will watch it complete there
old.S2-R12: Once the lines have been added, the inspection will no longer count as needing a work order. Drafting alone does not change that state, because a draft the user abandoned left the findings unactioned
old.S2-R13: If lines have already been added from this inspection, the user will be asked to confirm before adding a second set. The check is made when Add Lines is pressed, on the state at that moment
old.S2-R14: The destination will be chosen from a menu on the build action itself rather than from a dialog raised before it. The menu lists this work order — by number and status — and a new one seeded with the customer and unit. Either target goes straight to the drafting
old.S2-R15: A destination that cannot take lines will keep its place in the menu and say why. A destination that silently stops being offered reads as a fault
old.S2-R16: The build action will have one appearance wherever it is met — the ShopCoach purple with the AI badge, labelled Build lines, with a chevron where it opens the destination menu
old.S2-R17: Every rule in this document that withholds an action is enforced by the server. A request made without the permission is refused, whatever the interface showed. Hiding a control is how a rule is presented, not how it is enforced. This is stated once and applies to every story — the build, the destination choice, the asset Inspections tab, template authoring and Preview. The precedent is SV-7932, where a view-only user could invoke the ShopCoach line builder because only the button had been hidden
old.S2-R18: A generated line never arrives as a Fixed Line Total line. It is an ordinary labour-and-parts line, and switching it to a fixed total stays a deliberate act afterwards. A fixed total requires labour plus parts to equal it exactly or the line cannot be saved, and a drafted line arrives carrying both figures
old.S2-N1: If the inspection is not completed, the build will not be offered
old.S2-N2: If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the build will not be offered
old.S2-N3: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the build will not be available from any entry point
old.S2-N4: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' enabled, the option to create a new work order will not be shown. They will only be offered the option to add lines to the open work order
old.S2-N5: If the user does not have 'See Financial Data' enabled, the build is still allowed and the money is not shown. The proposed-lines panel withholds the labour rate, the labour total and the part prices, and the withholding is enforced by the server rather than by leaving the fields out of the markup. Everything else in the panel stays editable and the lines can still be added
old.S2-N6: If the shop has no labour types, the build will not run. A work order line cannot be created without a labour type or a fixed price, and S2-R18 forbids a generated line from being a Fixed Line Total, so the action states the reason rather than producing a line that cannot be saved
old.S2-E2: If a note is very long, it is given to ShopCoach whole rather than truncated before it is read
old.S2-E3: An inspection with thirty flagged findings is built without a cap and without an extra confirmation. If the assistant cannot draft that many in one run, the run is split rather than the surplus findings being dropped (S15-R14)
old.S2-E4: If the user chose to add lines to the open work order and it was closed by someone else in the meantime, the system tells the user and creates nothing
old.S2-E5: If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted before the user confirms, the build fails without creating a partial result
old.S2-E6: If two users draft from the same inspection at once, nothing is duplicated by the drafting itself, because a draft is not a work order line. Duplication happens only if both press Add Lines, which is accepted and recoverable
old.S2-E7: If the inspection is reopened by someone else while a draft is on screen, the draft stays usable and any lines already added are kept
old.S2-E9: If the lines were built onto a new work order and that work order is later deleted, the inspection counts as needing a work order again. The inspection itself is unaffected, because it belongs to the work order it was run on
old.S2-E12: If the work order the inspection was run on is deleted, the inspection survives it (S5-R21) and stays listed on the asset with a dash in its work order column. Where the lines had been added to that same work order they are gone with it, and the inspection counts as needing a work order again
old.S2-E10: Reversing an invoice does not change the inspection's state, because the work order and its lines still exist
old.S2-E11: If the lines built from an inspection are deleted while the work order remains, the inspection stays actioned and does not return to needing a work order. Deleting a work order is usually a correction; deleting a line is somebody who read the proposed work and decided against it, and re-raising the flag would ask them to do it again
old.S3-R1: The completed inspection screen will offer a Build lines action
old.S3-R2: The action will run the build described in S2, including the choice of target work order
old.S3-R3: The action will be usable on a phone, and the technician will be able to complete the whole flow without switching device
old.S3-R4: The screen will lead with a summary card: the completion line, a count per verdict, and a findings list naming each flagged position as field, axle, row and position with the reading that earned it
old.S3-R5: A verdict with no findings under it will not be counted on the card. A zero reads as a finding at a glance, which is the opposite of what it says
old.S3-R6: With ShopCoach the card's footer will offer View PDF, Go to work order and Build lines, and a note above it will name the product once. Without ShopCoach the footer will offer View PDF and Go to work order, and the same space will carry a plain line saying the findings are on the customer report and in the work order note feed and that the lines are added on the work order
old.S3-R7: The section-by-section review of what the technician entered will stay below the summary card. The card answers what happened; the sections answer what was entered. The service advisor, the inspection's start time and per-section progress are not carried onto this screen: the first two belong to the work order the inspection was run on, and progress means nothing once the inspection is locked
old.S3-N1: If the inspection has no Monitor or Not OK findings, the action will not be shown
old.S3-N2: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the action will not be shown. It will be absent, not disabled
old.S3-N3: If the inspection is not completed, the action will not be shown
old.S3-N4: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, no build action is shown. The screen offers View PDF and a link to the work order and nothing else — the action is absent, not disabled and not behind a tooltip (S2-R0)
old.S3-E1: If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, only the option to create a new work order is offered
old.S3-E2: If another user builds from the same inspection while this screen is open, the confirmation in S2-R13 is based on the current state rather than the state when the screen loaded
old.S3-E3: If the inspection is reopened while the screen is open, the action disappears
old.S4-R1: The inspection report note will offer a Build lines action alongside the existing view and download actions
old.S4-R2: The action will run the build described in S2, including the choice of target work order
old.S4-R3: The confirmation in S2-R13 will be based on the inspection's current state rather than on the note. The note reflects the inspection as it was when it completed, so a build performed elsewhere afterwards would otherwise go unnoticed and the same findings could be built twice without warning
old.S4-R4: All actions on the note will remain reachable on a phone, wrapping rather than overflowing
old.S4-N1: If the report recorded only passes, the action will not be shown
old.S4-N2: If the inspection has been deleted, the note remains as a record but the action will not be shown
old.S4-N3: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, the action will not be shown
old.S4-N4: If the note is being read in the work order's history view, the action will not be shown
old.S4-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, the note keeps its view and download actions and offers no build action (S2-R0)
old.S4-E1: If the work order itself is not an eligible build target, the build creates a new work order per S2-R5 and the note stays where it is
old.S4-E2: If the inspection was already built from through another entry point, the user is asked to confirm
old.S5-R1: An Inspections tab will appear on the asset record, alongside Work Orders, Invoices and Notes
old.S5-R2: The tab will list every inspection linked to that asset, most recently completed first
old.S5-R3: Each row will show the inspection, its status, the completion date, the technician who signed it, the findings, the work order it was run on, the report, and an action
old.S5-R4: The inspection column will show the template name with its version beneath, which is what distinguishes repeated runs of the same template
old.S5-R5: The status column will show the inspection's own progress only, and will not also express whether work is pending
old.S5-R6: The findings column will show one item per finding type with a colour, such as 1 Not OK in red and 3 Monitor in amber
old.S5-R7: The work order column will link to the work order the inspection was run on and show its status
old.S5-R8: The report column will link to the report when one has been generated
old.S5-R9: The action column will have three states. Needs action offers the build described in S6. Done shows the outcome and links to the resulting work order, reading "WO created" when a new work order was created and "Lines added" when the lines went onto the existing one. old.S5-R10: A filter row will offer All, Needs action, With issues and Not started, each with a count taken from the full list rather than from the filtered view
old.S5-R11: A summary will read "N of M need a work order"
old.S5-R12: An inspection needs action when it was completed after this release, has at least one Monitor or Not OK finding, and has not been built from. An inspection completed before the release is never flagged, because the data cannot tell one somebody already handled by hand from one nobody actioned. Those stay reachable through the With issues filter
old.S5-R13: Two users with different permissions viewing the same asset will see identical counts. Only the action button differs
old.S5-R14: Everything that navigates will be a link and everything that changes something will be a button
old.S5-R15: The tab will be usable on a phone. Every column's information will remain reachable and the page will not scroll sideways
old.S5-R16: The filter row will wrap on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and will keep its counts
old.S5-R21: An inspection records the asset it was run on, stored on the inspection when it is created rather than derived through its work order. old.S5-R17: A response contributes one count to exactly one of Pass, Monitor or Needs attention when the field is visible, the field is a checkbox or a measurement, and the response is Pass, Monitor or Not OK
old.S5-R19: N/A and unanswered responses contribute nothing
old.S5-R20: A per-axle measurement field contributes one count per axle, because each axle is a separate inspected position. A field with three axles marked OK, Monitor and Not OK contributes one pass, one monitor and one needs-attention
old.S5-N1: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — View' enabled, the Inspections tab will not appear at all. It will be absent, not empty
old.S5-N2: If the user has 'Work Orders — View' but not 'Customers — View', the asset record is unreachable and so is the tab. No alternative route is added
old.S5-N3: If the asset has no inspections, an empty state will explain so
old.S5-N4: If the user cannot build, the action column will show no button on any row
old.S5-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, the action column shows no build button on any row. The Needs action state described in S5-R9 does not arise (S2-R0)
old.S5-E1: For a not-started inspection, the completion date, technician and findings show dashes and no action is offered
old.S5-E2: A completed inspection whose responses are all N/A reads as having no issues and never needs action
old.S5-E3: If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, the inspection remains listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row remains usable. This requires an inspection to outlive its work order rather than being removed with it
old.S5-E4: If the asset has been moved to a different customer, all of its inspections are still listed. The tab is the asset's history
old.S5-E5: If the template has been archived or deleted, the row shows the template name and version as they were at the time, never "unknown"
old.S5-E6: If two inspections share a completion time, the order between them is stable rather than varying between loads
old.S5-E7: If the work order the lines were built onto is deleted and it is not the work order the inspection was run on, the row returns to Needs action rather than showing a Done state that points nowhere
old.S5-E8: An asset inspected weekly for three years has roughly 150 rows, which the list shows without paging. Above roughly 200 rows the list will need a date filter or paging, which is follow-up work
old.S6-R1: A row that needs action will offer a build action
old.S6-R2: The action will present the target choice up front as a menu rather than opening a dialog, because the user has already decided by the time they click
old.S6-R3: The menu is the shared destination menu of S2-R14, so the row offers the same two targets, worded the same way as every other entry point
old.S6-R4: The inspection's own work order is offered as a target only while it is an eligible build target, judged by its status on the row. When it is not, the target keeps its place and says why (S2-R15)
old.S6-R5: The action will run the build described in S2
old.S6-R6: A row that has been built from will show its outcome instead of the action
old.S6-R7: After a successful build, the row will leave the Needs action filter and the counts and summary will update with it
old.S6-R8: Eligibility here will be identical to S2-R5, including that Complete is not eligible
old.S6-N1: If the user does not have 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' enabled, the new-work-order target will not be offered anywhere on this tab
old.S6-N2: If the work order the inspection was run on is not an eligible build target, only the new-work-order target will be offered
old.S6-N3: If the user chose "Add lines" and the work order has since been closed, the system will explain that and create nothing
old.S6-N4: If the user does not have 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' enabled, no build action will appear on any row
old.S6-N5: If the organisation does not have ShopCoach, neither menu option is offered on any row and no build action appears on the tab (S2-R0)
old.S6-E1: If the work order the inspection was run on has been deleted, only the new-work-order target is offered
old.S6-E2: If several rows on the same asset need action, each is built separately. There is no bulk build
old.S6-E3: A user who can fill inspections but cannot create work orders, looking at a row whose work order is closed, has no available action. The row will show a dash with an explanation that creating a work order requires 'Work Orders — Create & Edit'. The explanation must be readable on a phone, where there is no hover
old.S7-R1: A note will be added to the work order the lines landed on, stating that it was built from the inspection
old.S7-R2: When the lines went onto a new work order, the note will link back to the work order the inspection was run on
old.S7-R3: The Notes tab count will include the new note immediately
old.S7-R4: An entry reading "Built from inspection" will be added to that work order's Audit Log
old.S7-R5: The Audit Log entry will name the inspection, link to it, and name the work order the inspection was run on
old.S7-R6: Both records will be written however the build was started, from S3, S4 or S6
old.S7-R7: The Audit Log entry and the note will carry the same three facts: that the work order was built from an inspection, which inspection, and which work order the inspection was run on. Whichever a user opens, they get the same account. Neither may carry a fact the other lacks
old.S7-R8: Both records will state how many lines were created, and the asset row will read "3 lines added" rather than "Lines added". The count is known when the record is written, and the scale of what was added is the first thing an advisor wants from it
old.S7-N1: If the lines went onto the work order the inspection was run on, the note will not link to that work order from itself
old.S7-N2: If the user does not have 'View History Logs' enabled, the Audit Log is not shown to them. The entry is still recorded
old.S7-E1: If either record cannot be written, the created lines are kept and the build still reports success. The lines are the valuable output
old.S7-E2: If a user deletes the note, the Audit Log entry remains
old.S7-E3: If the inspection is later deleted, the Audit Log entry keeps the inspection name as recorded, and the link fails gracefully rather than breaking the Audit Log
old.S7-E4: If the work order is later split, the note and the Audit Log entry stay on the original. The new work order carries no inspection provenance, because a split moves lines and does not copy records
old.S15-R1: The system will compose the brief it sends to ShopCoach from the inspection itself. For each Monitor and Not OK finding it will include the field label, its section, the measured value and its unit, the verdict, and the technician's note
old.S15-R2: A per-axle finding will name its axle and its measurement row, so a proposed line can be traced back to the measurement that caused it
old.S15-R3: The brief will state what ShopCoach may not do: invent a part it was not given, turn a passing finding into a line, or leave a flagged finding unrepresented
old.S15-R4: The user will never type anything to get lines. There is no prompt, no query box and no configuration step anywhere in this flow
old.S15-R5: The action that starts the build will read as an AI action before it is pressed, carrying the purple treatment and the AI badge. The label will not name the product
old.S15-R6: ShopCoach will be named once, at the step where the destination is chosen, and nowhere else in the flow
old.S15-R7: Drafting will start when the destination is chosen, so the navigation and the drafting happen together rather than one after the other
old.S15-R8: While the lines are being drafted, the panel will show one skeleton row per finding, because the number of findings is known before the drafted lines are
old.S15-R9: The work order will stay usable while the drafting runs
old.S15-R10: Cancelling during the drafting will leave the work order exactly as it was
old.S15-R11: Proposed lines will arrive selected, so the default is to accept them
old.S15-R12: Every proposed title, description, labour figure and part will be editable in place before the lines are added
old.S15-R13: Each proposed line will name the finding it came from
old.S15-R14: Every flagged finding will be represented by at least one proposed line however many findings there are. If the assistant cannot draft the whole set in one run, the set will be split across runs rather than the surplus being dropped
old.S15-R15: Nothing will reach the work order until Add Lines is pressed
old.S15-R16: The proposed-lines panel is shared with the Line Builder that is started from a work order with no inspection. A change made for this flow lands on that one too, and must not degrade it
old.S15-R17: The brief will be verifiable before release.
